question: Could within-assay native EMC GPNMB covariation with fixed ordinary myeloid RNA LST1/TYROBP/AIF1/CSF1R/CD68/FCER1G and stromal COL1A1/COL1A2/DCN/PDGFRA inform future localization sampling?
scope: Independent source-coverage and omission review only; no new quantities or statistics, no numeric authorization. Previously exposed GPNMB outcomes remain disclosed; this is not a cold discovery.
source_fields: Locked source metadata, published safe claim/method records, gene/probe annotation, first-column gene identities and headers only. No expression cells, rankings, image views or blocked-route repeats.
conditions: All13 Hofvander and six GSE24369 primary anticipated covariation contexts; complete10 GSE4303, four GSE28866 3SEQ and12 published TempO conditions assessed for measurement suitability, not dropped by old assay-estimator failures. Broader pending native/model/compartment conditions retain exact scope.
value: Bulk RNA association could nominate which measured cases and compartments to localize in a subsequent assay; it cannot identify cells, accessible protein, dependency or treatment benefit.
strongest_alternatives: A general myeloid or stromal bulk-mixture signature rather than an EMC-specific malignant-cell phenotype.
Capture/probe differences, handling, treatment/recurrence, small sample range, cross-study donor overlap and exposed selection.
Primary published correlation or use already answers the proposed scientific claim.
disproof_and_stop: No actual source-linked complete native EMC paired RNA feature measurements: no numeric stage.
Existing published same-disease covariation/use eliminates a useful new addition.
Annotation absence or ambiguity must be explicit; do not interpret no unique probe as biological absence.
Suitable accessible evidence remains pending and blocks promotion.
denied_scopes: FAP-tissue/glycan/HLA/structural genomics/fusion topology and sequence bodies remain closed.
ownership: This owned subtree only; integrating lead controls numerical authorization, shared mutations, main and push.
